subject: Helix Health — VPC/on-prem pricing & environment counts (post-call)
messages:
From: Jack Torre <jack.torre@helixhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 17:04:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: VPC/on-prem pricing — initial volumes and ask

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can align on pricing.

Summary:
- Use case: clinical summarization + retrieval for physician-facing app (PII redacted, enterprise-managed).
- Current expected steady-state: ~1M tokens/day (user prompts + model outputs). Spikes up to ~4M tokens/day during batch ingest windows. Monthly estimate: ~30M tokens (conservative). Attachment: Helix_Demand_estimate.xlsx with hour-by-hour sample.

Primary asks:
1) For a private/VPC deployment, what licensing model options do you recommend (annual/commit vs consumption)?
2) Target unit economics — we’re trying to hit ~600 USD / 1M tokens (bench target). Is that achievable with reserved capacity or on-prem?
3) Environment counts: we need guidance for dev/staging/prod sizing — we’re currently planning 8 prod nodes but want Redwood input.

Budget context: procurement flagged a 12-24 month budget band of $120k–$220k ARR for the infra piece (excluding implementation). We can be flexible if unit economics are attractive.

Next steps: Can you send a short pricing/option matrix and a baseline $/1M token estimate for each option? Also include support tiers and their response SLAs.

Thanks,
Jack
Head of Product, Helix Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jack Torre <jack.torre@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC/on-prem pricing — initial volumes and ask

Jack — great to meet. Appreciate the demand workbook. I pulled Ben (SE) and Laura (eng ops) into the thread to make sure we cover both the econ and environment sizing.

High-level options (brief):
- Option A — Private VPC (reserved capacity): Annual committed throughput + platform license. Best $/1M token when you commit; examples below. Includes standard support (business hours) by default, upgrade to Enterprise for 24/7 + named SLA.
- Option B — Dedicated on-prem (customer-hosted): Perpetual license + annual maintenance. Ongoing HW + ops cost is customer responsibility; Redwood provides software + 24/7 premium support as an add-on.
- Option C — Hybrid (VPC + on-prem fallbacks): Useful if you want burst isolation and local on-prem control for sensitive workloads.

Ballpark unit economics (based on 30M tokens/mo profile, seq lengths and KV cache assumptions):
- Reserved capacity (Option A): ~550–850 USD / 1M tokens depending on commit level and instance family.
- On-prem perpetual (Option B) effective amortized unit cost: highly variable; with typical infra amortized over 3 years, target range ~400–900 USD / 1M tokens (depends on hardware choices & utilization).
- Hybrid: usually mid-range between A & B, add ~10–15% for orchestration/licensing premium.

We can tune the numbers down with heavier KV caching, stricter batching, and model quantization recommendations — Ben will propose concrete scenarios.

Quick clarification questions for your procurement/engineering team to size a proposal: please confirm:
1) Final expected production count (you mentioned 8 prod nodes) — is that inference pods or physical GPU hosts?
2) Need for regulatory attestations (SOC2 Type II already mentioned?) and any required compliance add-ons.
3) Preferred support SLA (Standard (business hrs), Premium (24/7), Enterprise (named engineer + quarterly review)).

I’m attaching a short scenario doc (Redwood_VPC_Pricing_Scenarios.pdf) with sample price bands and what drives them. Ben — can you populate a quick three-scenario costing (low/median/high) based on Jack’s workbook?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Jack Torre <jack.torre@helixhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@helixhealth.com>, procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC/on-prem pricing — initial volumes and ask

Thanks Olga — answers below inline.

1) Production count: the "8 prod nodes" refers to inference pods (we run one pod per GPU host initially). We’ll likely provision 8 GPU hosts for prod. Staging: 2 hosts, Dev: 1 host. So environment count is Prod=8, Staging=2, Dev=1. Total GPU hosts = 11.
2) Compliance: SOC2 Type II in place; we will need Redwood evidence for data handling and endpoint logging for our auditors.
3) Support SLA: aiming for Premium (24/7) if price impact isn’t >15% of baseline.

Budget: procurement reiterated $120k–$220k ARR target for the infra/software piece. If reserved capacity can hit ~600 USD / 1M tokens (or less) with Premium SLA included, that will put us in the comfortable zone to proceed to procurement.

Also populating the demand workbook with a month-by-month ramp — see attached.

Jack

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jack Torre <jack.torre@helixhealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC/on-prem pricing — initial volumes and ask

Jack — thanks for the details. I ran three quick scenarios based on: (A) 11 GPU hosts (8P/2S/1D), (B) usage ramp (30M tokens/mo steady), and (C) Premium SLA. Attached is a short spreadsheet with cost lines; highlights below.

Scenario highlights (monthly averages, rounded):
- Scenario LOW (aggressive infra efficiency + quantized models): ~480 USD / 1M tokens — requires higher commit (12–24 month) and willingness to use our quantized runtime.
- Scenario MID (balanced): ~610 USD / 1M tokens — reserved VPC, Premium SLA, modest caching. This aligns with your target band around 600.
- Scenario HIGH (full redundancy + on-prem HA): ~920 USD / 1M tokens — perpetual + maintenance + ops assumed.

Recommended path to get into your procurement band (~$120k–$220k ARR):
1) Start with Reserved VPC commit (12 months) sized to 30M tokens/mo — pushes you into the mid scenario.
2) Add Premium SLA as an up-sell (expected +12% on software licensing line).
3) Run a 6-week optimization pilot: caching, quantization, and kernel tuning to target the LOW scenario if Helix is comfortable with model tradeoffs.

Action items I can deliver this week:
- Completed pricing scenarios spreadsheet (attached).
- Short bill-of-materials for 11 GPU hosts and recommended instance SKUs for on-prem sizing.
- A draft SOW for a 6-week optimization pilot (if you want us to price implementation).

Would you like a one-hour walk-through of the spreadsheet + BOM Friday morning? If procurement wants, I can also produce a condensed one-page quote for their review.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_VPC_Pricing_Scenarios.pdf, Helix_Demand_estimate.xlsx
